title: Fire-Resistant Sleeving and Seal Renewal at the Fwd Engine Mount Interface
abstract: Silicone-glass fire-resistant sleeving and a renewed seal set are introduced where the drain and vent lines cross the forward engine mount plane, after hot-section survey work showed local temperatures above the qualified limit of the previous sleeving.

sections.reason: A thermal survey flown on two development aircraft with additional instrumentation showed that the region immediately aft of the forward engine mount runs 40 to 55 degrees hotter in the cruise than the figure used to qualify the original sleeving. No failure had occurred, but the sleeving was outside its qualification envelope and a small number of operators had reported hardened and cracked sleeving at engine change. The powerplant integration office raised the change as an airworthiness housekeeping item rather than waiting for a finding.
sections.description: The drain and vent lines that cross the forward mount plane receive silicone-glass fire-resistant sleeving qualified to the higher temperature, retained by the existing standoffs. The interface seal D7120112839155 is replaced by a fluorosilicone item and the drain nozzle D7120115408026 gains a shorter, stiffer spigot so that the sleeve termination sits clear of the mount link D7120111938052. Detail is on drawing D71200052322. All of the work is inside the fan cowl in zones 456 and 462 and is done with the engine on the wing; the mount itself is not de-loaded. The seal fitting 93PP and the duct fitting 9634EN are disturbed and refitted with new hardware.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 0.9 kg per engine. No electrical load change. Interchangeable, and a mixed fit across the two engines of one aircraft is acceptable. The sleeving condition check at engine change is retained but its finding criteria are relaxed, and the fire zone integrity statement in the maintenance documentation is updated. Spares provisioning changes because the old sleeving reference is withdrawn from the catalogue.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in at MSN M00327 in April 2021. Retrofit is through Service Bulletin MRD-71-1006 and is an on-wing job of about six hours per engine with the fan cowls open, so most operators take it at the next scheduled cowl opening rather than as a separate event.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN M00327, absorbed in the engine build-up kit

title: Fire-Resistant Sleeving and Seal Renewal at the Fwd Engine Mount Interface

issue.reason: Combined embodiment package with the side link fitting change added, and the sleeve termination clearance restated as a measurement taken against the steel fitting boss.

Spares provisioning changes because the old sleeving reference is withdrawn from the catalogue at revision B.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in at MSN M00327 in April 2021. Retrofit is through Service Bulletin MRD-71-1006 and is an on-wing job of about six hours per engine with the fan cowls open, so most operators take it at the next scheduled cowl opening rather than as a separate event. Where an operator has embodied neither this change nor the side link fitting change of MOD-162044, the two are offered as one embodiment package: the fitting change needs the same mount joint opened with the engine off the wing, and an operator who plans them separately pays for the access twice. The sleeve termination clearance is re-measured against the fitting boss on each aircraft as part of the combined accomplishment.
